text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- Social and Health Ministry plans to split state-owned Alko to solve its problematic monopoly position: monopoly retail shops will be split from hotel and catering business and alcohol manufacturing.
- Having a role in developing tasks and organisation with employers increases workers' confidence, a study by the Finnish Metal Workers Union shows.
- Parliament is not interested in the environment and the current political atmosphere enhances negative discussion, says Pekka Haavisto, Minister of Environment.
- Alcoholism can be treated nowadays by drinking alcohol and taking medicine which takes the pleasure out of drunkenness, Finnish doctors treating alcoholism say.
KAUPPALEHTI

- Accelerating economic growth means unemployment will shrink faster that predicted; lowering income taxes would not cause imbalance in the economy because there are no signs of overheating, says Hannu Kaseva, economicst at the research Institute of Finnish Economy (ETLA).
- There is no reason for Amer K-shareholders to redeem their shares, says Heikki Kauppi, secretary general of the engineers' association and K-shareholders representative.
- Finland's relative price level is clearly above the average compared to other European Union countries, study by the OECD shows.
- Finnish construction companies should start looking at the vast opportunities in the Far East, sector representatives say.
AAMULEHTI
- While most of Finland is sweating in a heat wave, the ice is only just ready to break at Kilpisjarvi lake in northern Finland.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Obscurity in Raisio Yhtyma's partner negotiations for Benecol margarine has made international investors concerned and hurt share price.
- Moomin land says target of one million visitors may not be achieved this summer.
- Municipalities should build more houses for rental, but regulation of apartment rent prices is a outdated idea, Social and Health Minister Sinikka Monkare says.
DEMARI
- A separate bureau for children's issues should be created in the public sector, child protection associations urge.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Communists wanted to take power in the 1970, says historian Jukka Seppinen.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
